pulse_train.statement: A repeating pulse train does not evade the sustained ledger. (i) Between pulses the wall is absent, so a train with duty cycle D delivers at most D of the wall's effect while present only D of the time. (ii) Quantum interest (Ford & Roman): a negative-energy pulse must be followed (or preceded) by a positive-energy pulse that overpays it, and the required overpayment grows with the separation between the pulses -- an isolated negative pulse cannot be repeated for free; the long-time average energy density along an observer's worldline is constrained to be >= the sustained-type bound, so the time-averaged budget of an indefinite train is governed by W6's sustained law E_legal(L) = (3/(32 pi^2)) hbar c / L, not by the single-pulse tau^-4 bound evaluated at the short pulse width. Using the short-pulse bound for every pulse in an endless train double-counts the loophole.
